Research reported lint-hook-registration-paths.sh and lint-shellcheck.sh as has_test=false, which would have forced characterization tests before refactoring them. Hand-check found both DO have paired fixture suites (tests/test-lint-hook-registration-paths.sh 603L, tests/test-lint-shellcheck.sh 212L); the false negative is script-inventory.sh's own documented has_test caveat (it resolves tests/test-<basename> relative to the candidate's directory, i.e. scripts/lint/tests/, while the real suites live in scripts/tests/). All seven cluster members are therefore already fixture-tested and the whole first slice is unblocked with no characterization-test prerequisite.

The dispatch's recommended net-deletion floor of -10,000 non-test lines is not reachable from the clusters the dispatch itself enumerates. Measured at plan time: the seven-lint cluster is 3,318 lines of which roughly half is comment/blank (lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh 668 total / 338 code; lint-hook-registration-paths.sh 614 / 352), and the shared skeleton is ~112 shared code lines per pair, bounding the cluster's extractable net at roughly -700 to -1,000. install/uninstall-extension (543L), the typst pair (1,133L) and literature-search.sh (1,634L) together bound at roughly -800 to -1,350. Production-script net ceiling is therefore roughly -1,500 to -2,400, not -10,000. The deletable volume of that magnitude lives in the test corpus (121 core suites / 60,852 lines, all 121 redefining pass()/fail(), 115 redefining mktemp -d teardown) and in the markdown/context corpus the dispatch explicitly leaves untracked. Raised as a non-blocking user_decision on .return-meta.json; plan Phase 2 derives the per-cluster figures mechanically before any target is committed.

Post-deploy verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow run (triggered to sync the deployed .claude/ tree with source-store edits for test-script-inventory.sh's deploy-tree-first resolution) surfaced 2 pre-existing failures unrelated to this task's Phase 1 edits: (1) doc-lint Rule S finding on agent-system/extensions/lean/context/project/lean4/patterns/measurement-harness-strictness.md missing an index.json entry, and (2) eager-load total (67088B) exceeding the recorded baseline (66100B) for commands/orchestrate.md / skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md. Both are from concurrent in-flight work on other tasks, not from script-inventory.sh/verify-deploy.sh/test-script-inventory.sh changes. Not fixed here; out of scope for task 328.

SHELLOPTS is inherited from this harness's invoking shell into every bash subprocess, including errexit, even when a script's own header declares only 'set -uo pipefail' (no -e). A new test case assigning a potentially-failing command substitution directly (var="$(cmd)") silently killed the whole test script mid-run with no visible error, mimicking a crash rather than a reported FAIL. Diagnosed via bash -x tracing; fixed by wrapping the assignment in set +e / set -e 2>/dev/null || true, matching the existing defensive convention already used elsewhere in the same test file. Recorded so a future test-authoring pass does not re-debug the same symptom.

script-inventory.sh's --size-line (and full JSON) enumeration is git-ls-files-based and only sees TRACKED files; a newly-created, not-yet-staged file is invisible to it, silently undercounting a phase's NET-PROD/NET-TEST delta until git add is run. Discovered when Phase 3's new lib/lint-corpus-scan-lib.sh did not change the probe's scripts= count until staged. Confirmed the effect directly (staged vs unstaged runs) and recorded a measurement-methodology note in the plan's Phase 3 section for future phases.

lint-corpus-scan-lib.sh's extraction from two cluster members (lint-state-writer-boundary.sh, lint-directory-pathspec-boundary.sh) produced byte-identical whole-corpus --verbose finding output before and after migration (1336 files checked, 0/0 violations, exempted counts matching exactly), with the only textual diff being each lint's own self-referential EXEMPT line number shifting as an expected consequence of the file's line count changing. The nameref-based (local -n) function signature, modeled on the existing lib/gate-registry-lib.sh convention, composed cleanly with both the fast (shared-corpus-cache) and fallback (find-based) paths on the first attempt once the smoke tests passed.

This dispatch's Prior Decisions block carries a cycle-1 answer (2026-10-16T16:18:35Z) that explicitly keeps markdown/context OUT of scope, while the same dispatch's Description carries a later, dated operator decision ('SCOPE WIDENED TO KEEP THE -10,000 FLOOR, operator decision, 2026-10-16') that reverses exactly that clause and instructs 'PLAN REVISION REQUIRED'. Two authoritative inputs in one dispatch file disagreed. Resolved by the later-dated, more specific operator instruction and recorded in the plan's own 'Floor-shortfall decision' paragraph rather than silently picking one; .decisions.json was left untouched since it is a historical record of what was answered when.

The markdown-corpus scope widening was groundable mechanically in one revision round rather than needing a research dispatch: a 5-line shingling pass over all 927 markdown files produced the per-role duplicate-block table, and reading lint-agent-contracts.sh's four runtime fragment paths produced the gate-required exclusion volume. That yielded a measured eligible upper bound of 12,752 lines, so the declared -8,100 markdown target is a stated 64% capture rate against a measurement instead of a guess.

A naive markdown consolidation would have broken gates: lint-agent-contracts.sh reads four canonical fragments at runtime and FAILs any in-scope agent contract NOT carrying a verbatim copy, and lint-postflight-boundary.sh asserts a literal '## MUST NOT (Postflight Boundary)' heading. That duplication is deliberate and gate-enforced, and collapsing it would change those gates' finding sets -- which this task's own invariant forbids. Measured at ~3,997 of the 16,851 removable lines. Recorded as a hard exclusion class in the plan, with the exclusion list required to be derived by reading the lint's own fragment paths rather than hardcoded.

Phase 4's Scope Hypothesis re-derivation found scripts/lib/common.sh already defined common_test_pass/_fail/_info (byte-identical to the plan's required PASS/FAIL/INFO trio) and common_repo_root, both unused by any of the 122 core suites. Extended common.sh with the 3 genuinely-missing pieces (common_test_repo_root, common_test_resolve_candidate, common_test_workdir_init) instead of creating a parallel scripts/lib/test-harness-lib.sh, avoiding a duplicate-library net-addition the task's own acceptance criterion is chartered to catch. Also found 33/121 suites already source common.sh for an unrelated reason yet still redefine pass/fail/info locally -- a smaller migration diff than planned for those 33 in Phases 6-8.

During Phase 6 harness migration, a line-start-anchored call-site rename regex missed pass/fail/info calls inside case-statement arms and single-line if/then/fi shapes in 3 of 18 suites. Once the local pass()/fail() definitions were deleted, the unrenamed calls fell through to the real UNIX 'pass' password-store binary on PATH, silently dropping assertion counts (one suite's PASSED dropped 28->5) rather than erroring loudly. Caught by the before/after output diff this phase's own verification criterion requires, not by bash -n.

Phase 6's mandated before/after output diff on all 25 migrated test suites caught two migration-script defects (a brace-interpolation deletion-regex bug breaking bash syntax in 2 files, and the case-arm/single-line call-site rename miss in 3 files) before the phase closed, exactly as the plan's own acceptance criterion ('assertion count and PASS/FAIL case-name list must be identical before and after') intends. Both fixed prior to commit; final run-all.sh --only selection across all 25 suites plus test-common-lib.sh and test-lint-corpus-scan-lib.sh is 27 passed, 0 failed, 0 NEW.

A migration-script heuristic ('does this file mention lib/common.sh anywhere') wrongly treated 9 of 48 Phase-7 target suites as already sourcing the shared test harness, because they referenced lib/common.sh only as a fixture-copy source or dependency check, not an actual source statement. Removing their local pass()/fail()/info() definitions without inserting the real source line left common_test_pass/_fail/_info/_repo_root undefined at runtime; under set -uo pipefail (no set -e) each suite silently continued with 0 recorded assertions instead of crashing loudly. Caught by the mandatory before/after output diff (assertion counts dropped to 0), not by bash -n syntax checking. Fixed by restoring the 9 files from HEAD and re-running with detection narrowed to an actual top-level source/. statement naming lib/common.sh.

Beyond the planned pass/fail/info and REPO_ROOT migration, discovered a second widespread exact-shape duplicate pattern in Tranche B's pool: WORKDIR="$(mktemp -d)" + local cleanup() wrapper + trap cleanup EXIT, present byte-identically in 26 of the 48 target suites (a shape distinct from Phase 6's bare-trap pattern, so Phase 6's own migration did not already cover it). Verified each suite's cleanup() body was functionally equivalent to common_test_workdir_init's own trap body and that no suite invoked cleanup by name outside the trap, then collapsed all 26 triplets to a single common_test_workdir_init call, adding roughly -52 lines of net deletion beyond the pass/fail/info/REPO_ROOT work alone.
